title: Double granny square
subtitle: Two granny squares worked concentrically — one inside the other
excerpt: The double granny square nests a smaller granny motif inside a larger outer ring, with a visible border round separating the two. The inner and outer squares rotate 45 degrees relative to each other, giving a diamond-on-square layered effect when worked in two contrasting colours.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), concentric square chapter (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A double granny crochet square in cream inner square and sage outer ring on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Inner square rotated 45 degrees within the outer ring, 14 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished double granny square measures 14 × 14 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Double granny square
chartDefinition.caption: Inner square worked first (rounds 1–3). Transition round rotates orientation. Outer ring (rounds 4–6) locks around the inner square corners.

glossaryTerms.definition: Placing an inner motif at 45 degrees relative to the outer ring by working a transition round that picks up the mid-side points of the inner square as the new corners of the outer ring.

content.text: to nest the inner granny at 45 degrees inside the outer ring. The transition round picks up the chain spaces along the sides of the inner square — not its corners — as the new corner positions of the outer ring.
Work the inner square in colour A for three rounds. Work one transition round that locks the outer ring corners to the inner side spaces. Then work colour B for three outer rounds.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g colour A and 10 g colour B in DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work rounds 1–3 of the standard granny square in colour A. For the transition round: join new yarn at a corner ch-2 sp. *3 dc into corner sp. Ch 2. 3 dc into the next ch-1 side sp. Ch 2.* Rep from * around. These 8 ch-2 spaces become the corner positions of the outer ring. Work 3 more granny square rounds in colour B using these 8 corners — 4 true corners and 4 mid-sides — which sets the outer square at 45 degrees to the inner. Fasten off.
Try the join-as-you-go square to learn how to attach the outer ring of one motif to an adjacent motif on the final round rather than joining afterward.
